title: Nashville-Style Hot Fried Chicken
summary: Brined, double-dredged fried chicken dusted with cayenne and ghost chile as it leaves the oil. Very hot.

source.name: NYT Cooking (Melissa Clark, from Rodney Frazer)

ingredients.note: or 2 cups flour + 1/2 cup potato starch for a crisper crust
amount not given in the recipe; 2 to 3 is typical
about 2 inches deep in the pot

steps.title: Make the brine
steps.text: Whisk the salt and brine spices into the boiling water until the salt dissolves, then whisk in the ice water. It must be cold before the chicken goes in; chill it if not.

steps.title: Brine
steps.text: Submerge the chicken and refrigerate 2 to 6 hours.

steps.title: Mix the hot spice and dredge
steps.text: In one bowl, stir together the cayenne, ghost chile, and sugar. In another, mix the flour, granulated garlic and onion, salt, and pepper.

steps.title: First coat
steps.text: Pat the chicken dry, dust lightly with the hot spice, then with the dredge. Keep the rest of both. Refrigerate uncovered at least an hour so the coating sets.

steps.title: Heat the oil
steps.text: Heat 2 inches of oil to 325°F in a Dutch oven or heavy pot that has a lid.

steps.title: Second coat
steps.text: Whisk the eggs with the ice water. Dip each piece in the wash, coat again in the dredge, and shake off the excess. The egg wash gives a sturdier, crisper crust but can be skipped.

steps.title: Fry covered
steps.text: Fry 3 or 4 pieces at a time, lid on, until golden on the first side.

steps.title: Finish uncovered
steps.text: Take off the lid and keep frying, turning every 3 minutes, until evenly golden and cooked through, about 12 minutes total. Check the oil stays near 325°F between batches.

steps.title: Dust and rest
steps.text: Move the chicken to a rack over a sheet pan and dust it with the remaining hot spice while it's still hot from the oil.

notes: Brine and rest take at least 13 hours according to NYT, so start the day before. Traditionally served on soft white bread, which soaks up oil and tames the heat. Ghost chile is extremely hot; start at 1 tsp. Recipe uses both powdered and granulated garlic and onion; either kind works if you only have one.
